protocol: Fresh follow-up set frozen after the bounded-strategy prompt and response parsing were improved. It checks wording robustness on one fixed allocation pattern only; it is not an executable-workload, GPU-correctness, or universal generalization benchmark. Transient service failures may be retried up to twice, with every attempt recorded. Wrong or unsupported model answers are not retried.

cases.contract: For each query, output only the zero-based row number of its closest reference row. Resolve equal distances by taking the earliest reference row.
Return argmin(distance, dim=1): an integer vector with one nearest-reference position for each query.
The caller needs one reference index per query, selected by minimum Euclidean distance; no distance values are part of the result.
Produce the closest reference's input row ID for every query, using first occurrence when there is a tie.
For each query, return an integer count of reference points at distance less than or equal to radius 1.0.
Output one total per query for all reference points in the closed Euclidean ball of radius R; here R equals 1.0.
Count how many reference rows satisfy distance(query, reference) <= 1.0, separately for every query.
Return exactly N integers. Entry i is the number of reference points no farther than one unit from query i.
Return the three nearest reference indices for each query in increasing distance order.
Return each query's minimum distance as a float; the index is not needed.
Return the nearest reference row number if its distance is below one, and -1 otherwise.
For each query, output true if at least one reference is within radius 1.0, false otherwise. Do not output counts.
